transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Voss (Redwood SE), Hannah Chen (Redwood CSM), Jamal Price (Cobalt - Head of ML Ops), Priya Nair (Cobalt - Platform Eng), Elliot Graham (Cobalt - CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick QBR-style checkin; prioritize runway/cost savings and reliability fixes after recent spike. Agreed to run short pilot on Dedicated capacity and share pricing/security docs.

00:00 Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, appreciate it. we wanted to run through the runway and the reliability notes you sent. um jamal, do you want to kick off with what you saw over the black friday window?
00:18 Jamal Price: yeah thanks lena. so we had two major things: volume spiked ~4x from baseline and we saw a bunch of p99 tail-latency hits around 200 to 800 ms extra for generation calls, which caused some gating in our checkout flow. the cost also went way up, obviously. we think some of it is batch misconfig and a bunch of cold kv-cache misses, but we're not 100% sure.
00:40 Marcus Voss: yeah uh that matches what we saw in the traces you sent. there are a few long GC like pauses in your client side and some backend queueing when concurrency hit ~120. also there were a handful of model fallbacks to a lower-quantized variant — i saw references to "redwood dedicatedy- small" in the logs which i think is an artifact of the routing policy hitting a cost-tier.
01:05 Priya Nair: quick clarification — when you say fallbacks, are those automatic? we didn't expect model switching mid-request.
01:12 Marcus Voss: good q — the platform will route to fallback model family when the primary pool is out of capacity or the policy says to prefer lower-cost variants under high load. it shouldn't switch mid-request normally, but if a request gets routed to a different pool on retry you can see what looks like a fallback in the logs.
01:28 Elliot Graham: so is that something we can turn off? we want predictable latencies for checkout.
01:33 Lena Ortiz: yes you can pin a model version and set routing policies to strict — that's what customers on Dedicated typically do. the tradeoff is cost and how much headroom you reserve.
01:45 Jamal Price: right, we want to talk about reserved capacity. we looked at your dedicated pricing but want clarity on burst behavior and autoscaling.
01:53 Hannah Chen: i can cover the SLA bits — Dedicated comes with a baseline throughput SLA, and there's an option for burst pools which are billed separately. we'll share the exact pricing sheet after this call.
02:06 Priya Nair: regarding the p99s, what are the common mitigations? we already use prefix caching on some routes but maybe the kv cache isn't primed.
02:15 Marcus Voss: priming the KV cache is low-hanging and we can help script a priming run. also smarter batching and sequence-length caps — i noticed some long tokens per request that extend generation time. Quantization profile changes can also shift latency/cost tradeoffs, but that sometimes increases hallucination risk.
02:38 Jamal Price: can you explain the quantization tradeoff again? last time it seemed like we lost a little quality.
02:43 Marcus Voss: yeah in our experience, 4-bit/QLoRA style quantization will reduce memory and inference cost notably, but you might see small regression on edge-case outputs and slightly different tokenization behavior. for checkout prompts it's usually fine, but for your internal returns Q&A we should test.
02:59 Elliot Graham: another security question: we need to make sure logs are scrubbed and KMS is used for keys, and ideally we host in our VPC. also compliance.
03:08 Hannah Chen: totally. we'll send the SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide. Private deployment is possible; Private + VPC/on-prem options exist, but there are longer lead times and separate pricing.
03:20 Jamal Price: what's the typical lead time for private?
03:23 Lena Ortiz: for VPC-managed private control plane it's usually 6–8 weeks after contract; on-prem packaging can be longer. Dedicated setup is much faster, usually 1–2 weeks for reserved pools depending on region.
03:36 Priya Nair: ok. for the pilot we want to validate: stable p95/p99 under 150 ms, max cost delta < 20% vs current spike, and no model fallback during peak. is that reasonable?
03:48 Marcus Voss: yes that's a concrete set. we can run a short 48h pilot on Dedicated with your production traces replayed or with a live-headed traffic mirror. we'll aim to produce detailed tokens/latency/cost breakdown.
04:03 Jamal Price: live traffic mirror would be ideal, less configuration. can we keep it shadow mode so it doesn't affect checkout?
04:09 Marcus Voss: absolutely — shadow mode is standard. we can do 10% of traffic to start.
04:15 Priya Nair: about cost, will dedicated actually lower our unit cost at 4x spike?
04:20 Lena Ortiz: depends — if you commit to capacity you get lower per-token pricing but you pay for reserved headroom. for short spikes, burst pools are cheaper than a full month of reserved capacity. we'll run a cost model for your exact traffic shape.
04:34 Elliot Graham: are there any hidden fees? logging retention, debug traces?
04:37 Hannah Chen: there's optional long-term observability retention which is an add-on. default logs and traces are included for the retention period in the package. we'll call that out in the pricing sheet.
04:48 Jamal Price: okay timeline: jamal/priay will provide traffic p95/p99 and token volumes by monday; redwood will send pricing and security docs by tuesday; mark a pilot kickoff for week of dec 15.
05:04 Lena Ortiz: yeah i'll send the committed pricing and a sample contract. marcus will own the pilot run and share raw logs. hannah will send security artifacts.
05:12 Priya Nair: one more small item — can you give us the list of connectors for KMS and which cloud regions support dedicated right now?
05:19 Marcus Voss: sure i'll include AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a note on HSM options. Dedicated is available in us-west-2, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 for now; we can talk region expansion if needed.
05:33 Jamal Price: nice. any blockers from redwood's side to start pilot?
05:37 Lena Ortiz: no blockers. we'd just need the traffic sample and a signed statement of work / pilot acceptance.
05:44 Elliot Graham: okay good. let's recap the next steps.
05:47 Lena Ortiz: recap: 1) Cobalt to provide traffic metrics and a short sample replay or enable traffic mirroring (Priya/Jamal) by 2025-12-07. 2) Redwood to send pricing, pilot SOW draft, and security docs by 2025-12-09 (Lena/Hannah). 3) Marcus to run baseline 24h throughput tests and then pilot 48h mirror run, results due 2025-12-12. 4) schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2025-12-15.
06:25 Hannh Chen: sorry hannah typo there, but yes, will do.
06:29 Jamal Price: thanks everyone. that covers it.
06:33 Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread with links.
06:36 End of recording.
